analysis.title: Global Earnings Revision Ratio: Resilient earnings
key_insights: The Global Earnings Revision Ratio (upgrades vs downgrades) moderated from 1.03 to 1.01 in October but stayed above the 1.00 threshold where upgrades outnumber downgrades.
Developed Markets ratio is 1.14 versus 0.88 for Emerging Markets.
Japan's ratio fell from a record 2.36 to 1.94 but is still the highest among major regions. Its 3-month ratio is 2.18, and it improved the most over the month (+0.25).
The US ratio moderated from 1.18 to 1.01 and Europe's from 1.17 to 0.99. Asia Pac ex-Japan improved from 0.77 to 0.88.

Ratios for Global Semiconductors (1.29 to 1.33), Tech Hardware (1.63 to 1.68) and Software (0.93 to 1.15) improved despite weak AI-related stock performance. BofA suggests the weakness is driven more by sentiment than by changing earnings expectations.
Sector 1-month ratios are high for Banks (1.56) and Energy (1.47), and weak for Media (0.65), Telecom (0.71), Consumer Discretionary (0.72) and Consumer Staples (0.73).

By 3-month ratio, the strongest global sectors are Tech Hardware (1.90), Banks (1.59), Energy (1.57) and Semiconductors (1.57). The weakest are Consumer Staples (0.76), Consumer Discretionary (0.81) and Telecom (0.83).
In Asia Pac ex-Japan, Taiwan is highest at 1.56. Korea fell to a ten-month low (1.06 to 0.76), and China (0.78), India (0.81) and Australia (0.65) remain below 1.00.
Asia Pac ex-Japan sector ratios are highest for Energy (1.65), Tech Hardware (1.28) and Banks (1.11), and lowest for Telecom (0.45), Media (0.56) and Software (0.64).
Style 3-month ratios: Momentum 2.19, Growth 1.87, Quality 1.61, Risk 1.57, Dividend 1.36, Value 1.07, Size 1.00. Growth improved the most over the month (+0.36).
Large caps have a 3-month ratio of 1.58 versus 0.76 for the smallest stocks. The US 3-month ratio is 1.31 versus 0.75 for China.

The 3-month ratio is highest in Sweden (2.39), Japan (2.18) and Belgium (1.86). Sweden improved the most (+0.39). Germany (0.86) and the Netherlands (1.50) saw large 1-month drops, with the Netherlands falling to 0.80 in October.
Historically, the Global ratio correlates 0.59 with year-over-year MSCI AC World performance over 39 years. The US correlation is 0.36 and the Asia Pac ex-Japan correlation is 0.65.
Countries with a higher ratio have outperformed countries with a lower ratio over the long run.
At the current 3-month ratio range of 1.10-1.20, subsequent 12-month MSCI ACWI return is 5% on average. It is 3% when the ratio is rising and 7% when falling.

earnings_insights: Global Earnings Revision Ratio (consensus EPS upgrades vs downgrades, IBES data) was 1.01 in October 2026, down from 1.03 in September. The October reading is 'released' data.
US ratio fell from 1.18 to 1.01, and the US 3-month ratio is 1.31.
Asia Pac ex-Japan ratio rose from 0.77 to 0.88.
risk_factors: The Global ratio is only just above 1.00, so a further slip would put downgrades ahead of upgrades.
Korea's ratio hit a ten-month low of 0.76.
Ratios remain below 1.00 in China, India, Australia and the Emerging Markets aggregate.
Consumer, Telecom and Media sectors show broad downward revisions.
Weak AI-related stock performance could continue if sentiment, rather than earnings, keeps driving it.
